value: This article defines a field as a commutative ring where every non-zero element possesses a multiplicative inverse, tracing its historical development from Dirichlet and Dedekind to its modern generalization by Weber. A key focus is on various constructive notions of fields, such as discrete and Heyting fields, discussing their distinct implications in constructive mathematics and the internal logic of toposes, particularly regarding the real numbers. Additionally, the article examines the categorical properties of fields, noting that the category of fields, while finitely accessible, is unusual among algebraic structures for lacking completeness and cocompleteness.
